text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ontario urged to hand over services: Water, sewage, transit ought to be under municipal jurisdiction, panel says.
- Hockey lawyer Alan Eagleson expects charges: Legal cases pile up against ex-agent.
- Bob Dole beats bushes for last-minute support: Democrats worry that voters will not give Clinton clear mandate.
- Quebec's Lieutenant-Governor admits wearing swastika in 1942: Jean-Louis Roux says actions came out of 'student's mischievous desire to show off'
- Sale of Nelvana collapses: Officials will not say what scuttled proposed C$140-million deal with U.S. book publisher.
- Pranksters use Web to prick corporate egos.
- Fidelity's drive for dominance hits roadblock: Controversy over fund manager stalls fund's plans.

- Canadian Airlines turbulence hits Ottawa: Federal government rejects financial aid to airline but, with thousands of jobs at stake, election politics may force it to allow AMR Corp. to take control.
- Nelvana seeks 'alternatives' after Golden Books bails out.
